cells.tense: You're weighing now, and the scale is steady in your hand.
cells.verb: calibrating what's out of proportion until it sits right again
cells.place: where you see the shape of a thing without its story attached
cells.ask: offer this balance forward by letting one thing end when it's finished — honor the ending and trust what comes after it, so the exchange you keep fair can keep moving.
cells.core: You're weighing now, and the scale is steady in your hand. You can see what's out of proportion and you adjust it without keeping score — the correction is quick and then it's done. Nothing about this asks you to be clever; it asks you to be present to what's actually there, and you are.
cells.sheetLine: You see what's out of proportion and you set it right, without keeping score.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a debt that hasn't come due yet.
cells.verb: tallying who owes what before the exchange has even happened
cells.place: in a pattern you're tracking so closely the people in it have gone thin
cells.ask: let one load you're braced against stay unheld for a day — hold what's actually yours without forcing the rest into shape, and what comes back is fairness that flows instead of a ledger that balances.
cells.core: You're bracing for a debt that hasn't come due yet. The scale in your hand has become a ledger — every conversation gets totalled, every kindness weighed against what it cost you — and you're living ahead of the moment, ready for the imbalance before it arrives. The tracking is costing you the exchange it was meant to protect. What's out of proportion isn't them. It's how far ahead you're standing.
cells.sheetLine: You're tracking who owes what so closely the exchange itself has gone.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door you walked past a long time ago.
cells.verb: declining to claim what's owed you
cells.place: behind the point where you stopped seeing the pattern at all
cells.ask: keep one small practice without forcing it — repetition that doesn't strain, solitude that connects instead of hides — and what comes back is the plain sense of what's right, give and take moving again.
cells.core: You're still standing at a door you walked past a long time ago. Somewhere back there, claiming what you were owed made things worse, so you stopped claiming — and the stopping worked well enough that you call it patience now. You can still see the shape of unfairness, honestly, better than most. You just don't move toward your own side of the scale. The seeing hasn't gone anywhere. The asking has.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see what's unfair. You've stopped claiming your side of it.

cells.tense: The pen is down, and you're already writing.
cells.place: in a pattern you're reading clearly and calling it just how things are
cells.ask: name one thing you've been quietly keeping score on, out loud, once — and let your own sense of it land without defending it, so fairness can flow again instead of tallying in the dark.
cells.core: The pen is down, and you're already writing. You've been tallying — small grievances, small imbalances, the ones you'd never call grievances — and the count is running in you while you describe yourself as someone who doesn't keep score. You see the pattern in other people clearly enough to name it. In your own hand, it reads as just how things are.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping score in a column you don't know you're writing.
